# Appendix B — Software and reproducibility {#sec-appx-b}

## The series pattern

The analysis is a `{targets}` pipeline [@targetsr] in R, with `{renv}`
pinning package versions and one function per target. Paper 6 has its own
pipeline script and its own store, `_targets_p6.R` and `_targets_p6`,
following papers 4 and 5, so nothing it does can invalidate or overwrite the
published work of papers 1 to 5. `tar_config_set()` is never called anywhere
in paper 6: the setup chunk passes `store =` to each `tar_load()`, leaving
the project-root `_targets.yaml` that papers 1 to 3 share untouched.

Upstream objects — the runner table, paper 3's test key, paper 5's validation
scoring, fitting-partition fit, slice definition, test predictions and
published backtests — are read from the main and paper-5 stores
**read-only**, with their content hashes recorded in
`p6_upstream_fingerprint`. An upstream change therefore invalidates this
paper's downstream work rather than leaving it silently stale.

Every number in this document is read from a target at render time via
`tar_read()` or `tar_load()`. None is transcribed.

## No fitting

Paper 6 fits nothing. Both prediction sets already existed as paper-5
targets:

- the search set is `p5_scored_v7`, paper 5's rung-3b arm scored on the
  validation slice by the fitting-partition fit, with the series' own market
  probabilities already attached;
- the test split is `p5_test_predictions$rung3b`, the full-training-split
  refit's scoring, exactly as paper 5 published it.

Before anything is read off the search set, `p6_validation_predictions()`
asserts that paper 5's stored rung-3b validation PL loss equals the published
`r sprintf("%.6f", p6_fit_provenance_tbl$val_pl_loss[1])` and that the frame
is row-identical to paper 5's validation key. If it did not match, the search
set could not be attributed to the fit paper 5 selected, and the function
stops rather than continuing.

## Gates

Four standing checks run on the pipeline graph, not as afterthoughts.

`scripts/verify_p6_ledger.R` — six assertions on the ledger, unchanged from
the first attempt at this paper. Three that it rebuilds paper 5's published
test backtest exactly under S1/K0, both against the stored targets and
against the printed figures; one that the corrected each-way payout
reproduces paper 2b's when given paper 2b's terms; one that the corrected
terms move exactly the rows the field-size ladder marks; one that a staking
rule changes stakes and not the bet set. Also on the graph as
`p6_ledger_gate`.

`p6_search_set_check` — row identity of the search set against paper 5's
validation key, zero overlap with the test split, and zero overlap with the
fitting races the model was trained on.

`p6_contrast_check` — paper 5's rung-1 rule, that a compared pair differs in
exactly one term, asserted over every contrast the paper reads before
anything is scored. The two-stage design (@sec-stages) exists so that every
contrast is of that shape.

`p6_declaration_frozen` re-reads `DECLARED_RULES.md` from disk on every build
and matches it against the declaration target, so the committed artefact and
the pipeline cannot drift apart. `p6_declare_step()` errors rather than
returning if no candidate survives the eligibility gate for some bet type.

## Order of operations

The declaration was committed before any test target existed. The git history
records it: the commit introducing this version of `DECLARED_RULES.md`
contains no stage-2 target, and the stage-2 targets were added in the
following commit. The `_targets_p6` store was also destroyed and rebuilt
before that commit, so no test object from the superseded attempt survived
into this one. That is the only mechanism available for a claim of this kind
— a pre-registration living in the same repository as the analysis is only as
good as the history that timestamps it.

## The superseded attempt

An earlier version of this paper searched the rules on training-split
predictions, which are in sample, and is kept unrendered at
`papers/06_betting_strategy/SUPERSEDED/` with a README recording what was
wrong with it. It is not part of this paper and none of its numbers are
cited here. The ledger, the settlement, the eligibility machinery's
`p6_assert_one_difference()`, the fair-book columns and the margin
decomposition carried over from it unchanged.

## Running it

```
"C:/Program Files/R/R-4.6.0/bin/Rscript.exe" scripts/run_p6_pipeline.R
```

from the project root, via PowerShell — the database connection fails under
the Git Bash environment on the development machine. An optional argument
names a target to build up to, which is how the declaration was frozen before
the test targets were written.
